title: ‘One Day at a Time’: Inside an IDP Camp in Myanmar, Survival Is a Daily Challenge
gist: A field report from the Old Kran Khun IDP camp in Rakhine State shows displaced families exhausting savings, foraging depleted hills, and facing shrinking aid, water shortages, child dropout and airstrike risk, with Myanmar's military burning villages near Sittwe to deny the Arakan Army a base.

themes.theme: Displacement driven by military scorched earth

insights.claim: The Myanmar military torched Kyar Ma Thout village near Sittwe on February 6, 2024 and other settlements to deprive the Arakan Army of a base in the city's suburbs and secure Sittwe, one of only three of Rakhine's 17 townships it still controls.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Burn-and-clear tactics mean displacement will keep growing as long as the military holds Sittwe.

insights.claim: An estimated 100,000 people live in 93 IDP camps in Arakan Army-held areas and another 100,000 shelter in monasteries and relatives' homes, per the ULA, though these figures could not be independently confirmed.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Scale of the humanitarian caseload in AA territory; figures come from a party to the conflict.
insights.locator: Old Kran Khun camp is one of 93

insights.claim: Displaced families are burning through savings: a once-affluent Sittwe businessman's 1 million kyats lasted a month and about half his gold has been sold, leaving roughly a year of runway with no identified income source.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Savings depletion points to rising dependence on aid as reserves run out.

insights.claim: A family of four spends about 60,000 kyats a day on food while the household's foraging income sometimes does not exceed 10,000 kyats, and the nearby hills are being depleted by scavenging.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Income-expenditure gap of up to 6x shows food insecurity is structural, not temporary.

insights.claim: The ULA restricted logging five months before the report because of rapid deforestation of the hills IDPs rely on for firewood and vegetables.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Environmental limits are now constraining the camp's main informal livelihood.

insights.claim: Markets near the camp close for days after airstrikes or shelling, cutting incomes and food consumption.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Violence cuts the camp's remaining market access, compounding food insecurity.

insights.claim: Funding from global organizations to Rakhine IDP camps has decreased drastically over the past year, including due to a crackdown on networks that remitted funds, according to a ULA humanitarian official; truck water delivery stopped early this year as funds shrank.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Aid retrenchment and remittance-channel enforcement are directly worsening conditions.
insights.quote: Funding from global organizations has decreased drastically over the past year owing to many factors, including the crackdown on the networks that remitted funds

insights.claim: Ponnagyun camps lack water: groundwater lies about 600 feet deep, wells and ponds fall in winter, residents haul water from the Kaladan River 500 meters away between December and April, and turbid water drives skin disease, diarrhea and rainy-season malaria.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Water and disease risk escalates in the dry season and as camps grow.

insights.claim: About a quarter of camp residents are children and one-third of them have opted out of school, with only four families agreeing to enroll children after an NGO campaign and at least 20 children quitting from fear of airstrikes.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Education loss creates a long-term human-capital hit for Rakhine.
insights.locator: A Third of All Children Have Opted Out of School

insights.claim: On October 4-5 airstrikes on two Ponnagyun IDP camps killed at least eight IDPs and injured 13; the ULA claimed 16 killed and 40+ injured in earlier air attacks, unverified independently.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Attacks on camps show escalating air campaign against AA-held areas.

insights.claim: Old Kran Khun camp, housing 1,643 people in about 400 huts, has only three small communal trenches because there is no space and digging was never implemented, leaving residents to flee at the sound of jets.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Bhattacharyya
insights.so_what: Civilian protection gaps are acute and will worsen with any new strikes.
